messages:
Maya: Heads-up — while testing route-affinity canary, I saw two fallback events where requests moved to a lower-tier model because of quota. Console shows 'fallback' but not why. Can we emit richer telemetry so the permissions/quotas UI surfaces reason?
Evan: +1. We currently log event type = 'fallback' and route_id. No quota_id or entitlement check result.
Sam: Quick question: do we want this on the metrics pipeline or in the event audit stream? Both have tradeoffs.
Priya: For UX, the Console needs a short reason (quota_exceeded / permission_denied) and a link to the audit entry. Also show offending principal and role.
Evan: Proposed schema:
```json
{
  "event": "route_fallback",
  "route_id": "r_123",
  "reason": "quota_exceeded",
  "quota_id": "q_default_per_min",
  "effective_role": "tenant_reader",
  "actor": "user:alice@acme.com",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-20T14:12:03Z"
}
```
Sam: That makes sense. Implementation note: adding quota_id requires a call to quota-service during evaluation — could add a cheap boolean plus sampled quota_id to keep tracing volume low.
Maya: For rollout UX, can we show aggregated counts / grouped by reason and route over the canary window? e.g., 5 quota_exceeded, 2 permission_denied.
Priya: Yep — and highlight routes where grant changes during canary caused spikes.
Evan: API debate: do we attach this telemetry at authz-layer (authz-service emits event) or at router (router sees fallback and emits)? I prefer authz-service since it has role context.
Sam: Authz emits richer context but router has immediate visibility. Maybe both: authz emits canonical event; router emits lightweight 'fallback-observed' with ref to canonical event id.
ops-bot: smoke-deploy: canary rollout started for route r_123 (ver 1.2.0) :rocket:
Maya: OK let's do this plan: (1) Evan add schema to authz-service; (2) Sam add sampled router emission; (3) Priya updates Console to show reason + link. Target: next canary. Anyone object?
Priya: No objections. I'll draft Console mockups.
Evan: I'll open a PR for schema + event producer.
Sam: I'll add router flag for sampled fallback emit; will try to keep CPU cost <1%.
Maya: Thanks. If we can get one end-to-end smoke next week, great. :thumbsup:
